gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: We had five applications, but ___ of the candidates was suitable.
gaps.hint: more than two candidates + singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'None of the candidates was ...' is used for three or more; 'neither' is reserved for two.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: Every one of the switches ___ been tested twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: has.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of teenagers own a smartphone these days.
gaps.explanation: 'The majority of + plural noun' means most of them; 'the number of teenagers own' would be ungrammatical.
